items.title: Section: The Second Power — Seven Ways of Knowing Every Being's Karma, from Its Timing to Its Ripened Fruit

items.zh: 若有諸業已作、已增、已滅，名為過去。若有諸業非是已作、已增、已滅，亦非正作，而是當作，名為未來。若有諸業非是已作、已增、已滅，而是正作、正造、正為，名為現在。如是諸業品類差別復有三種。所謂身業、語業、意業。法受分別復有四種，如前廣說。謂有法受得現世樂，後苦異熟，乃至廣說。又此諸業現法當來有益無益加行差別，如應當知。若所造業依此方所，是名為處。若所造業以有情數、非有情數為所依事，是名為事。若所造業以不善根、或以善根為因緣起，是名為因。若所造業感愛非愛過失功德相應諸果，是名異熟。如是略說一切時分、一切品類、一切分位加行差別、一切方所、一切依處、一切因緣、一切過患及與功德。於此一切種類差別，皆如實知。是名如來自業智力。除此無有若過若增。
items.en:
Second, the power of wisdom regarding karma; first, distinguishing karma individually; first, classification by time. Karma already performed, increased, and extinguished is called past. Karma neither performed, increased, nor extinguished, nor presently being performed, but yet to be performed, is called future. Karma neither performed, increased, nor extinguished, but presently being performed, made, and done, is called present.
Second, classification by kind. Such karma further differs in kind into three: bodily karma, verbal karma, and mental karma.
Third, classification by circumstance and effort; first, circumstance. The distinction of felt experience is further of four kinds, as explained at length before: namely, feeling present pleasure with a later painful ripening, and so on at length.
Second, effort. Also, whether such karma proves beneficial or unbeneficial in this life or the next, in terms of effort, should be known accordingly.
Fourth, classification by location. Whatever place an action depends upon is called its place.
Fifth, classification by basis. Whatever being or non-being an action takes as its basis is called its basis.
Sixth, classification by cause and condition. Karma arising from unwholesome roots, or from wholesome roots, as its cause and condition, is called its cause.
Seventh, classification by fault and merit. Karma that ripens into a desirable or undesirable result corresponding to fault or merit is called its ripened fruit.
Second, concluding the essential meaning. In brief, understanding all of this — time, kind, circumstance and effort, location, basis, cause and condition, and fault and merit — exactly as it truly is, in every distinct category, is called the Tathāgata's power of wisdom regarding karma. Beyond this there is nothing excessive or additional.

items.zh: 有四靜慮、有八解脫，即由如是靜慮、解脫，心有堪能，心得自在，隨所樂事皆能成辦。

items.title: Section: The Third Power Opens — Equipoise and Attainment, and the Buddha's Own Radiance Preaching to the Brahmā Heavens

items.zh: 若隨彼彼色類差別三摩地相而入定時，當知說名等持、等至。如說世尊隨此色類三摩地相而入定時，如其定心，大光普照一切梵世妙音說法，但聞其聲，都無所見。乃至廣說。如是如來隨欲顯示彼彼事義，或共世間、不共世間，隨此色類三摩地相而入定時，速疾能辦。當知此中，即由靜慮、解脫勢力，心得自在。心自在故，依止於心，隨所樂事一切成辦。齊此名為修靜慮者一切所作，除此無有若過若增。如來於此靜慮所作一切種類，皆如實知，是故唯說靜慮、解脫、等持、等至。
items.en:
Second, equipoise and attainment; first, stating the name. Whenever one enters concentration according to whatever particular form-based object marks the concentration, know this is called equipoise or attainment.
Second, citing the teaching. It is said that when the Blessed One enters concentration according to such a form-based object, in accordance with his concentrated mind, a vast radiance universally illuminates [beings], and a wondrous voice proclaims the dharma; yet they only hear the voice, seeing nothing at all — and so on at length.
Third, concluding the meaning. Thus the Tathāgata, wishing to reveal whatever matter, whether shared with the world or not shared with the world, swiftly accomplishes it upon entering concentration according to such a form-based object.
Second, showing there is nothing beyond or additional. Know that it is precisely through the power of absorption and liberation that the mind attains mastery; because the mind is mastered, relying on the mind, whatever one wishes to accomplish is accomplished. This exhausts everything a practitioner of meditative absorption does; beyond this there is nothing excessive or additional. The Tathāgata, with respect to every kind of activity within meditative absorption, knows it exactly as it truly is; therefore it is said that only absorption, liberation, equipoise, and attainment are spoken of.

items.title: Section: Four Kinds of Affliction and Purity in Meditation, Provisional Names, and the Limit of Ever-Deepening Mastery

items.zh: 又若略說此靜慮等有二雜染。一者、為得所未得中障礙雜染，謂無方便善巧加行，及以諸蓋隨一現行。二者、已得所應得中自地雜染，謂煩惱纏及以隨眠。如是清淨復有四種。與上相違，應知其相。又即如是諸靜慮等種種引發假立名字，隨其色類如應安立，是名建立。又即如是諸靜慮等具證得已，後更勝進修習圓滿，得隨所欲、得無艱難、得無梗澁，是名清淨。如來於此，如其未得、如其已得，於所得中，若劣、若勝、若彼假名、若彼所有增進邊際，如是一切皆如實知，故說如來普於一切靜慮、解脫、等持、等至，得無上智。
items.en:
Second, explaining the wisdom attained regarding them; first, distinguishing the characteristics individually; first, regarding what is not yet attained and what is attained; first, presenting the affliction. In brief, these absorptions and their kin have two kinds of affliction. First, the obstructive affliction in striving to attain what is not yet attained: lacking skilful means for proper effort, or having any one of the hindrances currently manifest. Second, the affliction native to one's own level within what has already been attained: the outbursts of affliction together with their latent tendencies.
Second, giving the corresponding purity. Such purity likewise has four kinds, the opposite of the above; its characteristics should be understood accordingly.
Second, regarding their provisional names. Also, these various absorptions are given provisional names according to the particular form-based object that arouses each, as is fitting; this is called establishment.
Third, regarding their progressive refinement's furthest limit. Also, once these absorptions have actually been realised, further progressive cultivation brings them to complete mastery, attaining exactly what one wishes, without difficulty, without any obstruction; this is called purity.
Second, concluding the essential meaning. The Tathāgata, with respect to all this — whether not yet attained or already attained, whether inferior or superior within what is attained, together with their provisional names and the furthest limit of their progressive refinement — knows all of it exactly as it truly is; therefore it is said that the Tathāgata attains unsurpassed wisdom, universally, regarding every absorption, liberation, equipoise, and attainment.

items.title: Section: The Fourth and Fifth Powers — Ranking Beings' Faculties by Vehicle, and Reading Their Resolute Inclinations

items.zh: 如所成熟修證圓滿，信等五根成軟中上，當知是名諸根勝劣。若從他信以為其先，或觀諸法以為其先，成軟中上愛樂印解，當知是名種種勝解。
items.en:
Fourth, the power of wisdom regarding superior and inferior faculties. According to how a being to be matured realises the fruit of practice in full, the five faculties of faith and the rest mature into inferior, middling, or superior grades; know this is called superior and inferior faculties.
Fifth, the power of wisdom regarding various resolute inclinations. Whether arising first from faith in another, or first from contemplating phenomena, an inferior, middling, or superior grade of delighted, confident understanding is established; know this is called various resolute inclination.

items.title: Section: The Sixth and Seventh Powers — Every Being's Karmic Seeds, and Every Path Leading to Every Destination

items.zh: 若廣建立種種種性，或諸聲聞所有種性，或諸獨覺所有種性，或諸如來所有種姓，或有種種不定種性，或貪等行差別道理，乃至有情八十千行，當知此中名種種界。若即如是諸趣入門隨順正行，如貪行者修不淨觀，如聲聞地已廣宣說。當知此等名遍趣行。復有異門。謂趣一切五趣之行，當知此等名遍趣行。復有異門。謂依種種黨類差別，更互相違，各各異見、異欲諍論、互相違背諸外道類，即諸沙門、或婆羅門所有諸行；或餘一切品類差別此世他世無罪趣行；當知此等名遍趣行。如迦羅摩經等廣說。
items.en:
Sixth, the power of wisdom regarding various elements. Broadly establishing every kind of lineage — the lineage of śrāvakas, of pratyekabuddhas, of the Tathāgatas, or the various indeterminate lineages; or the distinct patterns governed by greed and the rest; extending to eighty thousand patterns of conduct among beings — know this is called various elements.
Seventh, the power of wisdom regarding the paths to every destination; first, explaining the name; first, the first meaning. This names the gateway practices according with the true path suited to each — such as one prone to greed cultivating contemplation on impurity, as explained at length in the Śrāvaka Ground; know this is called the paths to every destination.
Second, the second meaning. There is also another sense: this names the conduct leading to all five destinies; know this is also called the paths to every destination.
Third, the third meaning. There is also another sense: this names the conduct of the various conflicting factions among non-Buddhist teachers, each holding different views and desires, quarreling and opposing one another, whether ascetics or brahmins; or it names every other kind of conduct, within this life and beyond, that remains free of fault; know this is also called the paths to every destination.
Second, pointing [to the source]. This is explained at length in the Kālāma Sūtra and elsewhere.

blocks.text: The Buddha's powers to know beings' karma, their meditation, their faculties, inclinations, natures, and the paths that lead everywhere.

Karma already performed, increased, and extinguished is "past". Venerable Miào Jìng: yet it isn't wholly past, for the seeds remain in the mind. Master Cháng Bǎi: a living room or a temple hall: where good karma is done affects its weight.

Venerable Miào Jìng: in the story, only the voice of teaching was heard, no form visible at all. Master Cháng Bǎi: everyone heard the voice; no one saw the Buddha's body. (Untranslated, 0569c01: through the four meditations and eight liberations the mind becomes capable and free, able to accomplish whatever it wishes.)
Obstructive defilement before attainment; defilement native to the level after. Venerable Miào Jìng: inactive afflictions are latencies, active ones outbursts.
Venerable Miào Jìng: deep, unshaken understanding is 印, "seal".

Venerable Miào Jìng: 八十千 is eighty thousand; Master Cháng Bǎi speaks of eighty-four thousand distinctions in a moment. The path suited to each: impurity for greed; Venerable Miào Jìng, compassion for the angry type.
"It isn't wholly past, for the seeds remain." This is the Yogācāra view of karma in one sentence.

quiz.q: How does the treatise define past karma?
quiz.why: Karma already performed, increased, and extinguished is past. Venerable Miào Jìng: yet it isn't wholly past, for the seeds remain in the mind.

quiz.q: "The place an action depends on." What example does Master Cháng Bǎi give?
options: a living room or temple hall as places of good karma; the weight of karma varies by place
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: a living room or temple hall is where good karma is done; the weight of karma differs by place.

quiz.q: "They only hear the voice, seeing nothing." What do the lectures say?
options: Miào Jìng: only the sound, no form at all; Cháng Bǎi: all heard the voice without seeing the Buddha's body
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: only the voice of teaching, no form visible at all. Master Cháng Bǎi: everyone heard the voice, none saw the Buddha's body.

quiz.q: What are the two defilements of absorption?
options: obstruction to attaining (no skilful effort, hindrances) and defilement within what is attained (outbursts and latencies)
quiz.why: Obstructive defilement before attainment; level-native defilement after. Venerable Miào Jìng: inactive afflictions are latencies, active ones outbursts.

quiz.q: How many starting points of resolute inclination does the treatise give, and how do the lectures treat it?
options: two in the treatise: faith in another and contemplating phenomena; Cháng Bǎi also mentions entry through absorption; Miào Jìng reads 印 as unshaken understanding
quiz.why: The treatise gives two. Master Cháng Bǎi adds entry through absorption. Venerable Miào Jìng: deep, unshaken understanding is 印. The third gate, in the English note's "threefold gateway," comes from his lecture, not the treatise.

quiz.q: How many is "eighty thousand-thousand" 八十千? What do the lectures and English say?
options: Miào Jìng: 80 × 1,000 = 80,000, as the English; Cháng Bǎi says eighty-four thousand per moment
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: ten thousand is 十千; 八十千 is eighty thousand. Master Cháng Bǎi speaks of eighty-four thousand distinctions in a moment.

quiz.q: What is the second meaning of "paths to every destination"?
options: the conduct leading to all five destinies
quiz.why: The second meaning is the conduct leading to all five destinies. The first is the suited gateway, as impurity for greed; Venerable Miào Jìng: an angry type should instead cultivate compassion. The third is outsiders' conduct.

quiz.q: How do the lectures explain 黨 in "various factions"?
options: like-minded groups; people of one view forming parties, differing widely
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: a like-minded band. Master Cháng Bǎi: people of the same thinking form groups, with many differences between them.
